relationships.subject: high-fat diet
relationships.evidence_quote: Figure 4e shows higher levels of BH4 in the urine of the HFD-fed animals at 4 weeks [t(5) = 3.73; p < 0.01] and 8 weeks [t(4) = 3.32; p < 0.01] after the dietary intervention.

relationships.subject: high-fat diet
relationships.evidence_quote: The HFD-fed mice showed lower thresholds for mechanical hyperalgesia at weeks 2, 6, and 8 post-intervention (Figure 4d).

relationships.subject: physical exercise
relationships.evidence_quote: However, mechanical hyperalgesia was reduced at week 6 (Figure 7g) in the exercised mice submitted to the HFD [t(11) = 18.21; p < 0.01].

key_findings: High-fat diet increased mechanical and chemical hyperalgesia and urinary BH4 in mice; exercise reduced mechanical hyperalgesia.
Urinary BH4 proposed as a non-invasive biomarker of pain in obesity.
